failure_analysis.what: Replacing `for await` with an index-based `for` loop for Array inputs in LineIndex.build gave primary scores 0.880 / 0.887 / 0.882 (median 0.882) vs baseline 0.898. Correctness stayed 1 in all three runs. cur_median_mb_s was 493.68 / 514.32 / 515.68 against ref 563.00 / 577.03 / 581.51.
failure_analysis.why: The benchmark feeds about 16 chunks per 16 MB build, so the async-from-sync iterator wrapper and microtask hop cost a few microseconds per chunk against a build of roughly 30 ms. The per-byte scan loop dominates, with most bytes inside strings. The -0.016 gap to baseline is smaller than the ~4% run-to-run spread, so this is a null result, not a real slowdown. It matches the plan's own estimate of 0.85-0.95.
failure_analysis.lesson: Chunk iteration shape (for-await vs sync index loop) does not affect this benchmark. Round 1's sync scanChunk kernel (0.897) and the research brief's d1/d2 scratch runs showed the same thing. Future rounds should target per-byte work in the inner scan loop, mainly the in-string fast path, not per-chunk overhead.
